name: Niobium nitride
equilibrium_context: Tc about 15 K, conventional s-wave superconductor in the dirty limit

driven_states.emergent_property: Intense narrow-band picosecond THz pulses just below and above the gap frequency transiently increase the superconducting energy gap. The effect is particularly pronounced near Tc and is attributed to a non-thermal electron distribution that persists for about 100 ps.
driven_states.source: Beck et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 110, 267003 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.110.267003
driven_states.caveat: The THz-driven gap enhancement in NbN itself has not been independently reproduced; the underlying Eliashberg mechanism, however, has been in the microwave range. This concerns enhancement of an existing condensate below Tc, not the creation of superconductivity above Tc. No increase of Tc reported, only an increase of the gap.

threshold.quantity: frequency threshold relative to the gap frequency: enhancement below, pair breaking above

driven_states.measured_quantity: superconducting energy gap from the THz conductivity

sources: Beck et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 110, 267003 (2013), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.110.267003
gaps: Field strength specified instead of fluence, value not verified.
